Roadmap

Roadmap and gap register

What is done, what is next, the gaps we know about, and the work planned to close them.

Build phases

Each phase has an exit gate. A phase is not finished until its gate is met.

PhaseWorkExit gateStatus
0. Discovery and auditReconcile the blueprint with the live site and the existing courses; decide the six-level ladder.A ladder with honest statuses on the catalogue.Done
1. Foundations course (Level 1)Fourteen lessons, a lab, health check, certificate rule, curriculum map and five mock exams.Tests, build checks and browser checks pass; claims match the code.Done
2. Question bank growth and reviewGrow the bank, add question types, add papers four and five, and have every item reviewed by a person.Reviewer recorded for each item; chapter quotas met for every paper.In progress
3. Level 4: Agentic AI ArchitectureSixteen lessons, a lab with a seven-part health check, a rules checker and a tool contract checker. First edition.Every lesson has a lab that runs and sources with dates. Outside review is still to come (gap G11).Done
4. Level 5: Architecture Governance and EvolutionResearch, then write the lessons and lab, built on Levels 3 and 4.Every lesson has a lab that runs and sources with dates.Next
5. Level 6 and the lead architect portfolioLead architect practice, including a portfolio and oral defence design.Assessment design reviewed by someone outside Intellica.Planned
6. Platform foundationsOne portfolio across levels, recall scheduling and export.Automated tests, accessibility review and a restore test.Planned
7. Beta and external reviewPilot with learners and employers; independent curriculum and assessment review.Measurable learning gain and no critical defect.Planned
8. Credential launch and refreshPublish the scheme handbook, rules, verification, appeals and renewal; refresh mappings every year, including the iSAQB 2027.1 comparison.Governance operating and a legal review complete before the first award.Planned

Gap register

Found by reconciling the research blueprint with the live courses and with current sources.

GapFindingSourcePlanned work
G1. Question bank depthThe Level 1 bank is a first edition. It is smaller than the blueprint target and is the main limit on how many different mock papers a learner can take.Blueprint v2 target of 600 reviewed itemsGrow the bank in steps. 124 items shipped with checkpoint 36; checkpoint 44 raised it to 206 items and five mock papers, still far short of the target.
G2. Independent review of questionsItems were written and machine-checked. No human reviewer has read them yet, and correct options tend to be the longest.Blueprint v2 risk: weak question bankA person who did not write the items reviews every item against its learning goal. Record the reviewer and date.
G3. Question typesMost items are single choice. The real exam mixes types, so practice should too.Curriculum learning goals; external exam formatMore choose-several and allocation items, and scenario items that need a short reasoned choice.
G4. The 2027.1 release candidateThe candidate adds a chapter on AI. Lesson 13 already teaches verification and provenance, but it is Intellica extension content, not a match to the final goals.iSAQB RC1, 13 November 2026Run a formal comparison when the final text is published and update the lessons, bank and mock quotas.
G5. Curriculum goal 04-04 titleThe goal was added in 2025.1. Its title in our map is marked unconfirmed.Curriculum 2025.1-rev2Confirm the title against the official text and update the map.
G6. One portfolio across levelsEach course has its own lab record. Nothing yet links them into one portfolio.Blueprint v2 learner journeyA single architecture dossier that carries evidence from Level 1 to Level 6, with export.
G7. Levels 5 and 6 are not builtThe two levels have published outlines and no courses.Live catalogueBuild Level 5 next, then Level 6.
G8. Feedback from a personThe courses are self-study. Marking is by rubric and health checks, not by a tutor.Course pages and FAQOffer reviewed feedback on submitted work as a separate service, and say so plainly.
G9. No credential scheme yetOnly completion certificates exist, and they are self-reported. No assessors, moderation or appeals process exists.Blueprint v2 section 21; ISO/IEC 17024:2026 as a design benchmarkPublish competence standards, assessor rules, appeals and renewal before any credential is issued.
G10. External advanced routeThe academy does not prepare for the iSAQB Advanced assessment and does not claim to.iSAQB CPSA-A rulesDecide later whether to offer anything beyond pointing to the official route.
G11. Level 4 is a first edition without outside reviewLessons cite 2026 preprints and one press report with their limits stated. The labs have not been tried by learners. Some sources are cited from the author’s knowledge and marked as such.Level 4 course, 2026-11-27Have an iSAQB-experienced architect read the lessons and labs, and re-check every source marked "not re-read" before the next edition.

How releases work

  • Each release is a checkpoint with a changelog, a test run and a review date.
  • Existing course addresses, paid access and learner progress are never changed by an academy release.
  • Academy pages never state a price, a credential or a result that the live courses and the code do not support. A check fails the build if they disagree.

Reviewed 2026-11-25. Intellica is independent of iSAQB, arc42, ISO, IEC, IEEE and the Software Engineering Institute. Mappings show how our lessons relate to published topics. They are not an affiliation, an approval or a prediction of any exam result.
